units.title: Functions and Their Graphs
units.blurb: Combine, compose and invert functions, and use the graphs of the parent functions.

units.title: Quadratics and Complex Numbers
units.blurb: Extend quadratics with complex numbers, inequalities and new systems.

units.title: Polynomial Functions
units.blurb: Divide and factor polynomials, find their zeros, and sketch their graphs.

units.title: Rational Expressions and Functions
units.blurb: Simplify and combine rational expressions, solve rational equations, and graph rational functions.

units.title: Radical Functions and Equations
units.blurb: Work with nth roots, rationalize denominators, graph radical functions, and solve radical equations.

units.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
units.blurb: Use e and compound interest, understand logarithms, and solve exponential and log equations.

units.title: Sequences and Series
units.blurb: Write sequences recursively, use sigma notation, and sum arithmetic and geometric series.

topics.title: Parent Functions
topics.short: Know the shapes of x, x², x³, |x|, √x, ∛x and 1/x.

topics.title: Combining Transformations
topics.short: Apply stretches, reflections and shifts in the right order.
topics.trouble: Students shift before stretching inside the function, so 2(x − 3) is read as a shift of 6.

topics.title: Even and Odd Functions
topics.short: f(−x) = f(x) means symmetric about the y-axis; f(−x) = −f(x) means symmetric about the origin.
topics.trouble: Students decide even or odd from the exponents they see, missing that x² + x is neither.

topics.title: Adding, Subtracting, Multiplying and Dividing Functions
topics.short: Combine functions and find the domain of the result.
topics.trouble: Students forget that (f/g)(x) is undefined where g(x) = 0.

topics.title: Composition of Functions
topics.short: f(g(x)) feeds the output of g into f.
topics.trouble: Students multiply f(x) by g(x), or apply the functions in the wrong order.

topics.title: Inverse Functions
topics.short: An inverse undoes a function; its graph is the reflection over y = x.
topics.trouble: Students write f⁻¹(x) as 1/f(x).

topics.title: Checking Inverses by Composition
topics.short: f(g(x)) = x and g(f(x)) = x confirm an inverse pair.

topics.title: Restricting a Domain for an Inverse
topics.short: Keep one branch of a function so its inverse is a function.
topics.trouble: Students give ±√x as the inverse of x², which is not a function.

topics.title: Ramps: Building Bent-Line Graphs from ReLU
topics.short: ReLU(x) = max(0, x) is a ramp; sums of shifted, scaled ramps make any bent-line graph.
topics.trouble: Students read ReLU(x − 3) as bending at x = −3, or use the new slope as a ramp's coefficient when the coefficient is the change in slope at the bend.

topics.title: The Vertex Formula
topics.short: The vertex of ax² + bx + c is at x = −b/(2a).
topics.trouble: Students drop the negative sign, using x = b/(2a).

topics.title: Writing Quadratics from Points
topics.short: Build a quadratic from its vertex, its zeros or three points.

topics.title: The Imaginary Unit i
topics.trouble: Students multiply √−4 · √−9 as √36 = 6 instead of 2i · 3i = −6.

topics.title: Adding and Multiplying Complex Numbers
topics.short: Treat i like a variable, then replace i² with −1.
topics.trouble: Students leave i² in the answer or replace it with +1.

topics.title: Dividing Complex Numbers
topics.short: Multiply by the conjugate to clear i from the denominator.

topics.title: Quadratics with Complex Solutions
topics.short: A negative discriminant gives two complex conjugate solutions.

topics.title: Quadratic Inequalities
topics.short: Use the zeros and the graph to find where a quadratic is positive or negative.
topics.trouble: Students solve x² > 4 as x > ±2 instead of x < −2 or x > 2.

topics.title: Systems in Three Variables
topics.short: Eliminate one variable twice to reduce to two equations.
topics.trouble: Students eliminate a different variable from each pair, leaving two equations that still have three unknowns.

topics.title: Nonlinear Systems
topics.short: Solve systems with circles, parabolas and lines.
topics.trouble: Students lose solutions when they divide by a variable expression.

topics.title: Seeing Structure in Expressions
topics.short: Treat a chunk like (x + 1) or x² as a single quantity to rewrite an expression.
topics.trouble: Students expand everything first instead of noticing that x⁴ − 9 is a difference of squares.

topics.title: End Behavior of Polynomials
topics.short: The leading term decides what happens as x goes to ±∞.
topics.trouble: Students use the first term written instead of the term of highest degree.

topics.title: Zeros and Multiplicity
topics.short: A zero of even multiplicity touches the axis; odd multiplicity crosses it.
topics.trouble: Students think every zero is a crossing point.

topics.title: Polynomial Long Division
topics.short: Divide polynomials the way you divide numbers.
topics.trouble: Students skip a missing power instead of writing 0x², so the columns slip.

topics.title: Synthetic Division
topics.short: A shortcut for dividing by x − a.
topics.trouble: Students use −a instead of a when dividing by x − a.

topics.title: The Remainder and Factor Theorems
topics.short: p(a) is the remainder when dividing by x − a; p(a) = 0 means x − a is a factor.

topics.title: Sums and Differences of Cubes
topics.short: a³ ± b³ = (a ± b)(a² ∓ ab + b²).
topics.trouble: Students write the middle sign of the trinomial the same as the binomial's sign.

topics.title: Factoring Quadratic-Type Polynomials
topics.short: Treat x⁴ − 5x² + 4 as a quadratic in x².

topics.title: The Rational Root Theorem
topics.short: List the possible rational zeros p/q and test them.
topics.trouble: Students swap p and q, dividing factors of the leading coefficient by factors of the constant.

topics.title: Solving Polynomial Equations
topics.short: Factor completely and use the zero product property.
topics.trouble: Students divide both sides by x and lose the solution x = 0.

topics.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
topics.short: A degree-n polynomial has n complex zeros, counted with multiplicity.
topics.trouble: Students forget that complex zeros of real polynomials come in conjugate pairs.

topics.title: Writing a Polynomial from Its Zeros
topics.short: Multiply factors for each zero, including complex pairs, and scale to fit a point.
topics.trouble: Students write x + 3 as the factor for the zero 3, or leave out the conjugate of a complex zero.

topics.title: Sketching Polynomial Graphs
topics.short: Combine end behavior, zeros and multiplicity to sketch a graph.

topics.title: Polynomial Identities
topics.short: Prove identities and use them, such as making Pythagorean triples.

topics.title: The Binomial Theorem
topics.short: Expand (a + b)ⁿ with coefficients from Pascal's triangle.
topics.trouble: Students raise only the variables to powers and forget to apply them to the coefficients.

topics.title: Polynomial and Rational Inequalities
topics.short: Use a sign chart built from zeros and undefined points.
topics.trouble: Students multiply both sides by an expression whose sign they do not know.

topics.title: Simplifying Rational Expressions
topics.short: Factor, then cancel common factors, and note excluded values.
topics.trouble: Students cancel terms instead of factors, turning (x + 3)/3 into x.

topics.title: Multiplying and Dividing Rational Expressions
topics.short: Factor everything, then multiply as with fractions.

topics.title: Adding and Subtracting Rational Expressions
topics.short: Rewrite over a common denominator.
topics.trouble: Students add the denominators, or subtract only the first term of the second numerator.

topics.title: Complex Fractions
topics.short: Simplify fractions that contain fractions.

topics.title: Rational Equations
topics.short: Multiply by the common denominator, solve, and reject extraneous solutions.
topics.trouble: Students keep a solution that makes a denominator zero.

topics.title: Work-Rate and Average-Cost Models
topics.short: Model shared work and average cost with rational equations.
topics.trouble: Students add the times of two workers instead of adding their rates.

topics.title: Direct, Inverse and Joint Variation
topics.short: y = kx, y = k/x and y = kxz.

topics.title: Asymptotes and Holes
topics.short: Find vertical asymptotes, holes and horizontal asymptotes.
topics.trouble: Students put a vertical asymptote where a factor cancels, which is a hole.

topics.title: Graphing Rational Functions
topics.short: Use asymptotes, intercepts and sign to sketch the graph.
topics.trouble: Students think a graph can never cross its horizontal asymptote.

topics.title: Slant Asymptotes
topics.short: Divide when the numerator's degree is one more than the denominator's.

topics.title: nth Roots
topics.short: ⁿ√a is the number whose nth power is a.
topics.trouble: Students take an even root of a negative number as if it were real.

topics.title: Simplifying and Rationalizing Radicals
topics.short: Simplify roots and clear them from denominators.
topics.trouble: Students multiply only the numerator by the conjugate.

topics.title: Square Root and Cube Root Functions
topics.short: Graph and transform √x and ∛x.

topics.title: Radical Equations
topics.short: Isolate the root, raise both sides to a power, and check.
topics.trouble: Students square each term separately, or skip checking for extraneous solutions.

topics.title: Graphs of Exponential Functions
topics.short: Transform y = bˣ and find its asymptote.

topics.title: Exponential Equations with a Common Base
topics.short: Rewrite both sides with the same base and set exponents equal.

topics.title: Compound Interest
topics.short: A = P(1 + r/n)ⁿᵗ: interest earns interest.
topics.trouble: Students use the yearly rate for each period without dividing by n.

topics.title: The Number e and Continuous Growth
topics.short: Compounding more often approaches A = Peʳᵗ.

topics.title: What a Logarithm Is
topics.short: log_b(x) is the exponent you put on b to get x.
topics.trouble: Students read log₂ 8 as 2 · 8 or as 8/2.

topics.title: Switching Between Log and Exponential Form
topics.short: log_b(y) = x means bˣ = y.

topics.title: Properties of Logarithms
topics.short: Logs turn products into sums and powers into multiples.
topics.trouble: Students write log(a + b) as log a + log b.

topics.title: Change of Base
topics.short: log_b(x) = ln x / ln b.

topics.title: Graphs of Logarithmic Functions
topics.short: Graph y = log_b(x) as the reflection of bˣ.
topics.trouble: Students give the log graph a horizontal asymptote instead of a vertical one.

topics.title: Logarithmic Scales
topics.short: Each step on a log scale multiplies by the same factor, as in decibels and pH.
topics.trouble: Students think a pH of 4 is twice as acidic as a pH of 8, when it is ten thousand times as acidic.

topics.title: Solving Exponential Equations with Logs
topics.short: Take a log of both sides to bring the exponent down.
topics.trouble: Students divide by the base before taking logs, as if 3 · 2ˣ were 6ˣ.

topics.title: Solving Logarithmic Equations
topics.short: Combine logs, rewrite in exponential form, and check the domain.
topics.trouble: Students keep a solution that makes the argument of a log negative.

topics.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Models
topics.short: Model half-life, doubling time and pH.

topics.title: Choosing a Function Model
topics.short: Match data and situations to the right family of functions.

topics.title: Recursive Formulas
topics.short: Define a sequence by its first term and a rule for the next.
topics.trouble: Students mix up aₙ and aₙ₊₁ when writing the rule.

topics.title: Sigma Notation
topics.short: Σ is shorthand for adding the terms of a pattern.
topics.trouble: Students miscount the terms when the index does not start at 1.

topics.title: Arithmetic Series
topics.short: Add first and last terms, then multiply by half the number of terms.

topics.title: Finite Geometric Series
topics.short: S = a(1 − rⁿ)/(1 − r), and its use for loan payments.
topics.trouble: Students use n − 1 instead of n terms, or apply the formula when r = 1.

topics.title: Infinite Geometric Series
topics.short: When |r| < 1 the partial sums approach a/(1 − r).
topics.trouble: Students apply a/(1 − r) when |r| ≥ 1 and get a "sum" for a series that grows without bound.
